# The lcd349 C API

Generated from the public headers in `components/lcd349/include`, so it matches the code. Include `lcd349.h` only. Use LVGL 9 for the UI and these calls for everything physical; then a product builds unchanged for the board and the emulator.

## `lcd349.h`

lcd349: board SDK for the Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-3.49.

Include this one header. Products use LVGL 9 for the UI and this API for
everything physical; the same source builds for the board (esp32s3) and
the emulator (linux). See lcd349_core.h for the contracts every call keeps.

## `lcd349_core.h`

lcd349 core: version, errors, initialisation, status, time and memory.

Contracts that hold for the whole SDK:
- Every call returns an lcd349_err_t or a documented value, and never aborts
  on a hardware error (requirement 1.4).
- A subsystem that failed at init, or is absent, is reported by
  lcd349_board_status(), and its calls return LCD349_ERR_UNAVAILABLE.
- Callbacks run on a kit task (lcd349_ui or lcd349_evt, as documented per
  call), never in interrupt context (requirement 1.7).
- The same calls behave the same on the board (esp32s3) and in the emulator
  (linux target). Products never need a target check.

```c
#define LCD349_VERSION_MAJOR 0
#define LCD349_VERSION_MINOR 2
#define LCD349_VERSION_PATCH 0
#define LCD349_VERSION_STR "0.2.0"

typedef enum {
    LCD349_OK = 0,
    LCD349_ERR_ARG,         /**< an argument is invalid */
    LCD349_ERR_UNAVAILABLE, /**< the subsystem failed at init or isn't present; see lcd349_board_status() */
    LCD349_ERR_ON_USB,      /**< lcd349_power_off(): still running after the check delay, so USB powers the board */
    LCD349_ERR_TIMEOUT,     /**< the operation didn't finish in time */
    LCD349_ERR_IO,          /**< a bus, file or radio operation failed */
    LCD349_ERR_NO_MEM,      /**< out of memory */
    LCD349_ERR_NOT_FOUND,   /**< no such key, network or item */
    LCD349_ERR_STATE,       /**< not allowed now, for example before lcd349_init() */
} lcd349_err_t;

/** Returns a short constant name for err, such as "LCD349_ERR_ON_USB". Never NULL. */
const char *lcd349_err_str(lcd349_err_t err);

/** Subsystems, as bits in lcd349_board_status(). */
typedef enum {
    LCD349_SUB_POWER = 1u << 0,
    LCD349_SUB_DISPLAY = 1u << 1,
    LCD349_SUB_TOUCH = 1u << 2,
    LCD349_SUB_BUTTONS = 1u << 3,
    LCD349_SUB_BATTERY = 1u << 4,
    LCD349_SUB_AUDIO = 1u << 5,
    LCD349_SUB_RTC = 1u << 6,
    LCD349_SUB_STORAGE = 1u << 7,
    LCD349_SUB_WIFI = 1u << 8,
} lcd349_subsystem_t;

typedef struct {
    uint8_t backlight_pct;    /**< initial backlight, 0-100 */
    uint16_t touch_period_ms; /**< touch sampling period; 0 = the board's period */
    bool wifi_power_save;     /**< modem power save while connected */
} lcd349_config_t;

/** Default configuration: the board's backlight default and touch period, Wi-Fi power save on. */
#define LCD349_CONFIG_DEFAULT() {LCD349_BACKLIGHT_DEFAULT_PCT, 0, true}

/**
 * Brings the board up. On the board it asserts the power hold before anything
 * slow (requirement 1.3), then starts the display, touch, buttons, battery,
 * audio, RTC and storage, and the kit tasks lcd349_ui and lcd349_evt. Wi-Fi
 * starts only with lcd349_wifi_start().
 *
 * A subsystem that fails doesn't stop the others: check lcd349_board_status().
 * Call once, from app_main or a product task. cfg may be NULL for defaults.
 *
 * Returns LCD349_OK when the power hold and display are up (other failures
 * show in the status), LCD349_ERR_STATE if already initialised, or the
 * display's error.
 */
lcd349_err_t lcd349_init(const lcd349_config_t *cfg);

/** Bitmask of lcd349_subsystem_t values that failed at init. 0 = all good. */

/**

 * which the emulator doesn't simulate. Safe from any task, before init too.
 */

/** lcd349_time_us() in milliseconds, wrapping after about 49 days. */

/** Boot reasons, for crash detection. */
typedef enum {
    LCD349_BOOT_POWER_ON = 0, /**< cold start, or power-on in the emulator */
    LCD349_BOOT_SOFTWARE,     /**< esp_restart or an emulator reset */
    LCD349_BOOT_CRASH,        /**< panic or watchdog */
    LCD349_BOOT_BROWNOUT,
    LCD349_BOOT_OTHER,
} lcd349_boot_reason_t;

/** Why this boot happened. */
lcd349_boot_reason_t lcd349_boot_reason(void);

/** Memory capabilities for lcd349_alloc(). */
typedef enum {
    LCD349_MEM_INTERNAL = 1u << 0, /**< internal RAM: fast, scarce */
    LCD349_MEM_PSRAM = 1u << 1,    /**< external PSRAM: large, slower */
    LCD349_MEM_ANY = LCD349_MEM_INTERNAL | LCD349_MEM_PSRAM, /**< PSRAM first, then internal */
} lcd349_mem_t;

/**
 * Allocates size bytes with the given capability and counts it, so the
 * emulator can report usage against the board's budgets (requirement 3.13).
 * Returns NULL on failure. Free with lcd349_free(). Safe from any task.
 */

/** Frees memory from lcd349_alloc(). NULL is ignored. */

typedef struct {

    size_t psram_bytes;
    size_t internal_peak;
    size_t psram_peak;
    size_t largest; /**< largest single allocation so far */
} lcd349_mem_stats_t;

/** Fills stats with lcd349_alloc() usage. */
void lcd349_mem_stats(lcd349_mem_stats_t *stats);
```

## `lcd349_display.h`

Display and UI threading.

Products draw with LVGL 9 directly, in landscape 640x172. The kit renders
full frames, rotates them into the panel's portrait orientation, swaps the
RGB565 bytes and sends the result to the panel (or, in the emulator, to the
same framebuffer bytes), so both targets see identical pixels.

Threading: LVGL runs on the kit task lcd349_ui. Touch LVGL only
- inside LVGL callbacks (event handlers, timers), which run on lcd349_ui, or
- between lcd349_ui_lock() and lcd349_ui_unlock() from any other task.

```c
/** The landscape 640x172 LVGL display, or NULL before lcd349_init() or if the display failed. */
lv_display_t *lcd349_display(void);

/** Sets the backlight, 0-100 %. 0 is dark, and touch isn't read while dark (requirement 1.5). */
lcd349_err_t lcd349_backlight_set(uint8_t pct);

/** The current backlight level, 0-100. */
uint8_t lcd349_backlight_get(void);

/**
 * Puts the display to sleep (backlight off, rendering paused, touch not read)
 * or wakes it (backlight restored, the current screen redrawn). Touch never
 * wakes the display: wake it from a button handler.
 */
lcd349_err_t lcd349_display_sleep(bool sleep);

/** True while the display is asleep. */
bool lcd349_display_is_asleep(void);

/** Takes the LVGL lock. Recursive: safe inside LVGL callbacks. Never call from an interrupt. */
void lcd349_ui_lock(void);

/** Releases the LVGL lock. */
void lcd349_ui_unlock(void);

/**
 * Queues fn(ctx) to run on lcd349_ui with the LVGL lock held, and returns at
 * once. Use it to update the UI from network or timer tasks.
 * Returns LCD349_ERR_NO_MEM if the queue is full, LCD349_ERR_STATE before init.
 */
lcd349_err_t lcd349_ui_call(void (*fn)(void *ctx), void *ctx);

/**
 * Tags an object for the UI checker (requirement 6.4). Tags are short words:
 * "list-row" exempts a dense list row from the touch-target rule, and
 * "ignore:<rule-id>" silences one rule for this object. Call it several times
 * to add several tags. Tags show up in ui.tree, so exceptions are reviewable.
 * Call on lcd349_ui or with the lock held. Tags are removed with the object.
 */
lcd349_err_t lcd349_ui_tag(lv_obj_t *obj, const char *tag);

/** True if obj carries tag. */
bool lcd349_ui_has_tag(const lv_obj_t *obj, const char *tag);

/**
 * Copies obj's tags, comma-separated, into out (always NUL-terminated).
 * Returns the number of tags.
 */
size_t lcd349_ui_tags(const lv_obj_t *obj, char *out, size_t out_len);
```

## `lcd349_input.h`

Touch, buttons, and the button gesture classifier.

Touch is single-point, sampled every touch period while the display is
awake, and never wakes the device. Buttons are BOOT and PWR, debounced by
the kit. Holding BOOT through a reset enters the ROM download mode, so never
design a boot-time BOOT combination.

Subscriber callbacks run on the kit task lcd349_evt, in order. Keep them
short; to touch LVGL from one, use lcd349_ui_call() or the UI lock.

```c
/* ---- Touch ---- */

/** One touch sample in landscape coordinates (0-639, 0-171). */
typedef struct {
    uint16_t x;
    uint16_t y;
    bool pressed;  /**< false: the finger lifted; x and y repeat the last point */
    uint32_t t_ms; /**< lcd349_time_ms() when sampled */
} lcd349_touch_sample_t;

typedef void (*lcd349_touch_cb_t)(const lcd349_touch_sample_t *sample, void *ctx);

/** The LVGL pointer input device for the touch screen, or NULL if touch failed. */
lv_indev_t *lcd349_touch_indev(void);

/**
 * Subscribes to raw first-point samples: one per touch period while a finger
 * is down, plus one with pressed=false when it lifts. Up to 4 subscribers.
 */
lcd349_err_t lcd349_touch_subscribe(lcd349_touch_cb_t cb, void *ctx);

/* ---- Buttons ---- */

typedef enum {
    LCD349_BTN_BOOT = 0,
    LCD349_BTN_PWR = 1,
    LCD349_BTN_COUNT = 2,
} lcd349_btn_t;

/** A debounced button edge. */
typedef struct {
    lcd349_btn_t btn;
    bool down;
    uint32_t t_ms; /**< when the edge happened (start of the debounced transition) */
} lcd349_btn_event_t;

typedef void (*lcd349_btn_cb_t)(const lcd349_btn_event_t *ev, void *ctx);

/** Subscribes to debounced down and up edges of both buttons. Up to 4 subscribers. */
lcd349_err_t lcd349_buttons_subscribe(lcd349_btn_cb_t cb, void *ctx);

/** True while btn is held (debounced). */
bool lcd349_button_is_down(lcd349_btn_t btn);

/* ---- Gesture classifier (optional, pure: no tasks, no hardware) ----
 *
 * Feed it button edges and call lcd349_classifier_tick() regularly (every
 * 10-20 ms, for example from an lv_timer) while a button is down. It turns
 * edges into gestures:
 *   SHORT     released before the first hold threshold
 *   HOLD      still down and has just reached hold threshold `level` (1-based);
 *             use it to commit at the moment the hold completes
 *   HOLD_END  released after reaching threshold `level`
 *   CHORD     the second button went down within chord_window_ms of the first,
 *             before either reached a hold; both are then consumed until released
 *   CHORD_END both buttons are up again after a chord
 */

#define LCD349_CLASSIFIER_MAX_HOLDS 3
/** Room to pass for `out`: no call emits more gestures than this. */
#define LCD349_CLASSIFIER_MAX_OUT 8

typedef struct {
    uint16_t hold_ms[LCD349_CLASSIFIER_MAX_HOLDS]; /**< strictly ascending; 0 ends the list */
    uint16_t chord_window_ms;                      /**< 0 disables chords; must be below hold_ms[0] */
} lcd349_classifier_cfg_t;

typedef enum {
    LCD349_GESTURE_SHORT,
    LCD349_GESTURE_HOLD,
    LCD349_GESTURE_HOLD_END,
    LCD349_GESTURE_CHORD,
    LCD349_GESTURE_CHORD_END,
} lcd349_gesture_kind_t;

typedef struct {
    lcd349_gesture_kind_t kind;
    lcd349_btn_t btn; /**< CHORD and CHORD_END: the button that went down first */
    uint8_t level;    /**< HOLD and HOLD_END: 1-based threshold index; otherwise 0 */
    uint32_t t_ms;    /**< when the gesture happened */
    uint32_t held_ms; /**< SHORT and HOLD_END: how long the button was down; HOLD: the threshold */
} lcd349_gesture_t;

/** Classifier state. Treat the fields as private. */
typedef struct {
    lcd349_classifier_cfg_t cfg;
    uint8_t n_holds;
    struct {
        bool down;
        bool consumed;
        uint8_t level;
        uint32_t t_down;
    } b[LCD349_BTN_COUNT];
    bool chord_active;
    lcd349_btn_t chord_first;
} lcd349_classifier_t;

/** Initialises c. Returns LCD349_ERR_ARG if thresholds aren't ascending or the chord window isn't below the first. */
lcd349_err_t lcd349_classifier_init(lcd349_classifier_t *c, const lcd349_classifier_cfg_t *cfg);

/**
 * Feeds one debounced edge. Emits any hold reached before ev->t_ms first.
 * Writes up to max gestures to out and returns how many.
 */
size_t lcd349_classifier_feed(lcd349_classifier_t *c, const lcd349_btn_event_t *ev, lcd349_gesture_t *out, size_t max);

/** Emits HOLD gestures whose threshold has passed by now_ms. Returns how many. */
size_t lcd349_classifier_tick(lcd349_classifier_t *c, uint32_t now_ms, lcd349_gesture_t *out, size_t max);

/**
 * Progress toward btn's next hold threshold, 0-1000, for a fill bar.
 * 0 when the button is up or consumed by a chord; 1000 once the last threshold is reached.
 */
uint16_t lcd349_classifier_hold_permille(const lcd349_classifier_t *c, lcd349_btn_t btn, uint32_t now_ms);
```

## `lcd349_power.h`

Power, sleep and battery.

On battery the board stays on only while the power hold is asserted;
lcd349_init() asserts it first. Releasing it powers the board off, unless
USB is supplying power. Touch never wakes the board: only BOOT or PWR do.

```c
/** Asserts (true) or releases (false) the power hold. Releasing it on battery powers off. */
lcd349_err_t lcd349_power_hold(bool hold);

/**
 * Powers the board off by releasing the power hold. On battery this call
 * doesn't return. If the board is still running after the USB check delay
 * (LCD349_POWER_OFF_USB_CHECK_MS), USB is powering it: the hold is
 * re-asserted and the call returns LCD349_ERR_ON_USB (requirement 2.4).
 * Show the user something like "unplug USB to power off".
 */
lcd349_err_t lcd349_power_off(void);

/**
 * Light sleep until BOOT or PWR is pressed, or until timeout_ms passes
 * (0 = no timeout). The display sleeps first, and Wi-Fi stays associated with
 * modem power save. On a button wake, *woke_by (if not NULL) is set and the
 * press is also delivered as a normal button event, so a product can treat the
 * waking press as wake-only.
 * Returns LCD349_OK on a button wake, LCD349_ERR_TIMEOUT on timeout.
 * Call from a product task, not from lcd349_ui or lcd349_evt.
 */
lcd349_err_t lcd349_sleep_until_button(uint32_t timeout_ms, lcd349_btn_t *woke_by);

/** Where the board's power comes from (requirement 1.8). */
typedef enum {
    LCD349_POWER_SOURCE_UNKNOWN = 0, /**< the board can't tell, or before lcd349_init */
    LCD349_POWER_SOURCE_USB,         /**< USB is powering the board */
    LCD349_POWER_SOURCE_BATTERY,     /**< the battery is powering the board */
} lcd349_power_source_t;

/**
 * The power source, as the kit last saw it: it checks once a second, so a
 * change shows within about a second. Unlike lcd349_power_off(), this never
 * powers the board off to find out.
 *
 * On the board, USB means a USB host is connected: a charger with no data
 * (a wall adapter, a power bank) reads as BATTERY, though it charges the
 * battery. UNKNOWN when the board can't tell. The emulator reports its model
 * (lcd349 run --usb or --battery, and lcd349 state set).
 */
lcd349_power_source_t lcd349_power_source(void);

/** Called when the power source changes, with the new one. */
typedef void (*lcd349_power_source_cb_t)(lcd349_power_source_t source, void *ctx);

/**
 * Sets the one power-source callback (NULL removes it), replacing any
 * earlier one. It runs on the kit's event task, like the button and Wi-Fi
 * callbacks, once for each change; not when it is set.
 */
lcd349_err_t lcd349_power_on_source_change(lcd349_power_source_cb_t cb, void *ctx);

/**
 * Reads the battery: millivolts at the cell (averaged, divider applied) and
 * an estimated percentage from the discharge curve. Either pointer may be NULL.
 */
lcd349_err_t lcd349_battery_read(uint16_t *mv, uint8_t *pct);

/** Maps cell millivolts to 0-100 % with the board's discharge curve. Pure. */
uint8_t lcd349_battery_pct_from_mv(uint16_t mv);
```

## `lcd349_audio.h`

Tones on the board's speaker. Calls return at once; playback runs on a kit
task. A new tone or sequence replaces whatever is playing. In the emulator,
tones are recorded as events and played by the viewer.

```c
/** One step of a tone sequence. hz = 0 is a rest. */
typedef struct {
    uint16_t hz;
    uint16_t ms;
} lcd349_tone_t;

#define LCD349_TONE_SEQ_MAX 32

/** Plays hz for ms at volume 0-100. hz 20-20000; ms 1-10000. */
lcd349_err_t lcd349_tone(uint16_t hz, uint16_t ms, uint8_t volume);

/** Plays a sequence of up to LCD349_TONE_SEQ_MAX steps (copied) at volume 0-100. */
lcd349_err_t lcd349_tone_seq(const lcd349_tone_t *steps, size_t n, uint8_t volume);

/** Stops any tone. */
lcd349_err_t lcd349_tone_stop(void);
```

## `lcd349_kv.h`

Namespaced key-value storage that survives power-off: NVS on the board, one
file per namespace in the emulator (cleared by --wipe). Flash wears out, so
don't write on every event. Safe from any task.

```c
/** Longest namespace or key, in bytes (the NVS limit). */
#define LCD349_KV_NAME_MAX 15
/** Largest blob or string value, in bytes. */
#define LCD349_KV_VALUE_MAX 4000

/**
 * Reads a string. On entry *len is the size of out; on success it is the
 * length including the NUL. Returns LCD349_ERR_NOT_FOUND if absent, and
 * LCD349_ERR_NO_MEM (with *len set to the size needed) if out is too small.
 */
lcd349_err_t lcd349_kv_get_str(const char *ns, const char *key, char *out, size_t *len);

/** Writes a string. */
lcd349_err_t lcd349_kv_set_str(const char *ns, const char *key, const char *val);

/**
 * Reads a blob; *len works as in lcd349_kv_get_str(), without the NUL.
 * Values are typed: reading a string key as a blob, or a blob key as a
 * string, returns LCD349_ERR_ARG.
 */
lcd349_err_t lcd349_kv_get_blob(const char *ns, const char *key, void *out, size_t *len);

/** Writes a blob of len bytes. */
lcd349_err_t lcd349_kv_set_blob(const char *ns, const char *key, const void *val, size_t len);

/** Erases one key, or the whole namespace when key is NULL. Erasing what isn't there is OK. */
lcd349_err_t lcd349_kv_erase(const char *ns, const char *key);
```

## `lcd349_wifi.h`

Wi-Fi station. The radio is 2.4 GHz only: 5 GHz networks are invisible (a
phone hotspot must offer 2.4 GHz). Up to LCD349_WIFI_MAX_NETWORKS saved
networks in priority order; while disconnected the kit scans every
LCD349_WIFI_SCAN_INTERVAL_S seconds and joins the highest-priority one it
sees. Products use BSD sockets for network I/O; the SDK doesn't wrap them.

Event callbacks run on the kit task lcd349_evt.

```c
typedef struct {
    char ssid[33];
    char password[65]; /**< empty for an open network */
} lcd349_wifi_net_t;

typedef struct {
    char ssid[33];
    int8_t rssi; /**< dBm */
    uint8_t channel;
    bool secure;
} lcd349_wifi_ap_t;

typedef enum {
    LCD349_WIFI_IDLE = 0,     /**< stopped, or no saved networks */
    LCD349_WIFI_SCANNING,     /**< looking for a saved network */
    LCD349_WIFI_CONNECTING,
    LCD349_WIFI_CONNECTED,    /**< associated and has an IPv4 address */
    LCD349_WIFI_DISCONNECTED, /**< lost or failed; will scan again */
} lcd349_wifi_state_t;

typedef enum {
    LCD349_WIFI_REASON_NONE = 0,
    LCD349_WIFI_REASON_AUTH,      /**< wrong password */
    LCD349_WIFI_REASON_NOT_FOUND, /**< no saved network visible */
    LCD349_WIFI_REASON_LOST,      /**< connection dropped */
    LCD349_WIFI_REASON_STOPPED,   /**< lcd349_wifi_stop() */
} lcd349_wifi_reason_t;

typedef struct {
    lcd349_wifi_state_t state;
    lcd349_wifi_reason_t reason;
    char ssid[33];  /**< the network involved, or empty */
    int8_t rssi;    /**< dBm, when connected */
    uint32_t ip4;   /**< network byte order, when connected */
} lcd349_wifi_status_t;

typedef void (*lcd349_wifi_cb_t)(const lcd349_wifi_status_t *status, void *ctx);

/** Replaces the saved networks (copied, highest priority first). n <= LCD349_WIFI_MAX_NETWORKS. */
lcd349_err_t lcd349_wifi_set_networks(const lcd349_wifi_net_t *nets, size_t n);

/** Starts the station: scan, connect, reconnect. */
lcd349_err_t lcd349_wifi_start(void);

/** Stops the station and disconnects. */
lcd349_err_t lcd349_wifi_stop(void);

/**
 * Scans now and fills out with up to *n visible networks, strongest first;
 * *n is set to the number written. Blocks for a few seconds: call from a
 * product task, never from lcd349_ui or lcd349_evt.
 */
lcd349_err_t lcd349_wifi_scan(lcd349_wifi_ap_t *out, size_t *n);

/** The current state. */
lcd349_err_t lcd349_wifi_status(lcd349_wifi_status_t *status);

/** Subscribes to state changes. Up to 4 subscribers. */
lcd349_err_t lcd349_wifi_subscribe(lcd349_wifi_cb_t cb, void *ctx);
```

## `lcd349_console.h`

The serial console: the board's USB-C port (USB Serial/JTAG), or in the
emulator the pseudo-terminal `lcd349 run` publishes as the instance's serial
port. Write to it with printf or ESP_LOG; read lines a host tool sends with
lcd349_console_read_line(). Host tools see the same bytes either way.

```c
/** Longest line the console keeps, without its line ending. */
#define LCD349_CONSOLE_LINE_MAX 1023

/**
 * Waits up to timeout_ms for the next line from the host (0 = don't wait) and
 * copies it into buf without its line ending (LF, CR or CRLF), NUL-terminated.
 * A line longer than size - 1 bytes (or LCD349_CONSOLE_LINE_MAX) is cut and
 * the rest of it dropped. Lines arriving while nobody reads are kept up to a
 * small limit, then dropped, as a full receive buffer would.
 *
 * Works before lcd349_init(). Read from one task, and never from lcd349_ui:
 * it blocks.
 *
 * Returns LCD349_OK, LCD349_ERR_TIMEOUT, LCD349_ERR_ARG (buf NULL or size < 2),
 * or LCD349_ERR_UNAVAILABLE when the console can't be read.
 */
lcd349_err_t lcd349_console_read_line(char *buf, size_t size, uint32_t timeout_ms);
```

```c
/* Full-frame flush time in ms, used by the emulator's timing model. */
#define LCD349_FLUSH_MS 13
#define LCD349_FLUSH_MS_VERIFIED 1

/* Backlight PWM polarity: 1 = duty 0 is full brightness. */
#define LCD349_BACKLIGHT_ACTIVE_LOW 1

/* Touch: 1 point, never a wake source. */
#define LCD349_TOUCH_POINTS 1
#define LCD349_TOUCH_PERIOD_MS 30
#define LCD349_TOUCH_PERIOD_VERIFIED 1
#define LCD349_TOUCH_I2C_ADDR 0x3B

/* Each button's centre as a landscape x in pixels, from its position on the
 * case (millimetres from the active area's left) and the panel's pixels per
 * millimetre: put a button's on-screen hint under the button with these. */
#define LCD349_BUTTON_BOOT_X_PX 597
#define LCD349_BUTTON_PWR_X_PX 521

/* Pins (GPIO numbers). */
#define LCD349_PIN_BOOT 0
#define LCD349_PIN_EXPANDER_INT 42
#define LCD349_PIN_I2C_SCL 48
#define LCD349_PIN_I2C_SDA 47
#define LCD349_PIN_I2S_BCLK 15
#define LCD349_PIN_I2S_DOUT 45
#define LCD349_PIN_I2S_MCLK 7
#define LCD349_PIN_I2S_WS 46
#define LCD349_PIN_LCD_BACKLIGHT 8
#define LCD349_PIN_LCD_CS 9
#define LCD349_PIN_LCD_D0 11
#define LCD349_PIN_LCD_D1 12
#define LCD349_PIN_LCD_D2 13
#define LCD349_PIN_LCD_D3 14
#define LCD349_PIN_LCD_PCLK 10
#define LCD349_PIN_LCD_RST 21
#define LCD349_PIN_PWR 16
#define LCD349_PIN_TOUCH_SCL 18
#define LCD349_PIN_TOUCH_SDA 17

/* The TCA9554 I/O expander on the main I2C bus (LCD349_PIN_I2C_*): its
 * address, and the port bit (P0-P7) of each signal. */
#define LCD349_EXPANDER_I2C_ADDR 0x20
#define LCD349_EXPANDER_PIN_TP_INT 0
#define LCD349_EXPANDER_PIN_BL_EN 1
#define LCD349_EXPANDER_PIN_IMU_INT1 2
#define LCD349_EXPANDER_PIN_IMU_INT2 3
#define LCD349_EXPANDER_PIN_RTC_INT 4
#define LCD349_EXPANDER_PIN_LCD_TE 5
#define LCD349_EXPANDER_PIN_SYS_EN 6
#define LCD349_EXPANDER_PIN_NS_MODE 7

/* Other chips on the main I2C bus. */
#define LCD349_CODEC_I2C_ADDR 0x18
#define LCD349_RTC_I2C_ADDR 0x51
#define LCD349_IMU_I2C_ADDR 0x6B

/* Battery: ADC1_CH3 through a divider. */
#define LCD349_BATTERY_ADC_UNIT 1
#define LCD349_BATTERY_ADC_CHANNEL 3
#define LCD349_BATTERY_DIVIDER 3

/* Kit behaviour. */
#define LCD349_BACKLIGHT_DEFAULT_PCT 80
#define LCD349_BUTTON_DEBOUNCE_MS 10
#define LCD349_POWER_OFF_USB_CHECK_MS 1000
#define LCD349_WIFI_MAX_NETWORKS 4
#define LCD349_WIFI_SCAN_INTERVAL_S 60
#define LCD349_AUDIO_SAMPLE_RATE_HZ 16000

/* Design rule thresholds, as ui.lint checks them. Size UI with these, never
 * with copied numbers. */
#define LCD349_RULE_TOUCH_TARGET_PX 56
#define LCD349_RULE_FONT_MIN_PX 12
#define LCD349_RULE_CONTRAST_X100 450 /**< 4.5:1 */

/** One point of the battery discharge curve. */
typedef struct {
    uint16_t mv;
    uint8_t pct;
} lcd349_battery_point_t;

/** Something the emulator doesn't model, and how to check it on the board. */
typedef struct {
    const char *id;
    const char *what;
    const char *check_on_hardware;
} lcd349_fidelity_item_t;

/** The board's static description, generated from device/device.json. */
typedef struct {
    const char *name;
    const char *vendor;
    const char *soc;
    uint16_t cpu_mhz;
    uint8_t psram_mb;
    uint8_t flash_mb;
    uint16_t lcd_w;   /**< landscape width, as products draw */
    uint16_t lcd_h;   /**< landscape height */
    uint16_t panel_w; /**< panel-native width */
    uint16_t panel_h; /**< panel-native height */
    uint16_t ppi;
    float px_per_mm;
    float mm_w;
    float mm_h;
    uint16_t flush_ms;
    bool flush_ms_verified;
    uint16_t touch_period_ms;
    bool touch_period_verified;
    uint8_t touch_points;
    const lcd349_battery_point_t *battery_curve; /**< falling millivolts, 100 % first */
    uint8_t battery_curve_len;
    bool battery_curve_verified;
    const lcd349_fidelity_item_t *fidelity; /**< what the emulator doesn't model */
    uint8_t fidelity_len;
    const char *device_json_sha; /**< first 12 hex digits of device.json's SHA-256 */
} lcd349_board_info_t;

/** Returns the board's static description. Never NULL; safe before lcd349_init. */
const lcd349_board_info_t *lcd349_board_info(void);
```
